newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks mixed at close, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks mixed at close, seen consolidating.

text.p: Greek equities closed mixed on Monday, steadying after a weak start and brokers said the market was seen consolidating at current levels and might even recover some of the ground lost recently.

"The market lacks the momentum which was moving it a month earlier, but prices are entering a stage of consolidation, needed after this year's long-lasting rally," said George Politis, an analyst at EuroSec.
"The largest part of selling pressure on blue chips has been cushioned," said broker Lina Tseti at N.Devletoglou Securities.
The market may claw its way back in the following days as sidelined investors are monitoring market conditions to time the reinvestment of their liquidity, she added.
Market sentiment was not hurt by the sharp fall in prices in recent days.
"Investors are very resilient despite concerted selling pressure on large caps and no panic selling was observed, hence the low turnover," Tseti said.
Trading in OTE telecom, which plans a sizeable part-flotation and rights issue, remained active with around 215 thousand shares changing hands.

OTE signed on Monday a deal to acquire a 20 percent stake in Telekom Srbija, the telecoms utility of New Serbia, for 675 million marks, with Italy's telecoms holding company Stet buying a 29 percent stake for 893 million marks.
"OTE's public offering will top the success of last year's IPO with international institutional portfolios and domestic retail investors remaining keen on the issue," said Tseti.
"The greater part of the liquidity created by the market's 150-point drop recently will be channeled into the public offering and subsequently to the rights issue." EuroSec's Politis said.
The Athens general settled 0.16 percent or 2.56 points lower at 1,589.79 from Friday's 1,592.35 close.
It set an intra-day low at 1,565.01 and met resistance at 1,600 points, turning back from a high of 1,599.47.
Banks and industrials led the market's fluctuations but provided a sharp contrast at the close. Banks firmed 0.47 percent but industrials fell 0.82 percent.
Turnover reached a moderate 16.1 billion drachmas on volume of 3.86 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 121 to 92 with 21 shares unchanged on 234 traded.
